title: Braided Apple Walnut Bread
description: Apple, walnuts and cinnamon coconut sugar twisted into a honey-sweetened spelt bread wreath. Free of eggs and refined sugar.

items.note: added as needed; grams are for 1 cup of spelt. The source uses half spelt and half all-purpose overall
peeled, cored and chopped small (gala, fuji or granny smith)

step_groups.name: Dough
steps: Warm the milk, butter, sweetener and salt in a small saucepan (or the microwave) on low, just until the butter melts. Let cool until warm to the touch.
In a large bowl, combine the first-mix flour and the yeast. When the milk is warm, 120 to 130°F (49 to 54°C), pour it in slowly and stir until smooth and well blended, about 1 minute.
Switch to a dough hook (or a wooden spoon) and add more flour a little at a time until the dough is soft and pulls away from the sides of the bowl. You may not need all of it.
Knead until smooth, elastic, and soft but not sticky, about 4 to 5 minutes. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.

step_groups.name: Fill and shape
steps: Meanwhile, mix the coconut sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl.

Roll the dough into a large rough rectangle on a lightly floured surface, or on a large sheet of parchment so you can slide it onto a baking sheet later. Spread the softened butter over it and sprinkle evenly with the cinnamon sugar, then the apple and nuts.
Starting from a long edge, roll the dough up tightly like cinnamon rolls. Slice the roll in half lengthwise, leaving 2 to 3 inches (5 to 8 cm) intact at the top to hold it together.
Turn the halves so the filling faces up. Overlap one over the other repeatedly to make a twist, and pinch the ends to seal.
Bring the ends together into a wreath and tuck one end under the other.

step_groups.name: Rise and bake
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Slide the parchment with the wreath onto a baking sheet, or lift the wreath onto a parchment-lined or lightly greased sheet.
Cover with a clean towel or plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place for 25 to 30 minutes, until almost doubled.
Bake on the middle rack for 20 to 30 minutes, until golden brown. Let cool, then sprinkle with powdered sugar if you like.

storage: Best eaten the same day. Reheat leftover slices in the microwave for 20 to 45 seconds, or wrapped in foil in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 10 to 15 minutes.
